summary: The noun פֶּגֶר denotes the dead body of an animal or a person. The verb describes men too exhausted to continue a pursuit. The connection between these uses is uncertain.

senses.definition: The body of a dead person or animal.

evidence.note: After Abram lays out the animals, the bird of prey descends upon הַפְּגָרִים, their carcasses.
The people are told that their own bodies will fall in the wilderness.

senses.definition: To lack the strength to go farther.

evidence.note: Two hundred of David’s men stay behind at the Besor because they are too exhausted to cross it.
